bug_semantics: LiquidJS promised to bound each render with renderLimit, but Render.renderTemplates checked elapsed time only inside its loop over template nodes. An empty for or tablerow body parses to an empty templates array, so every attacker-controlled collection iteration calls renderTemplates([]), executes no check, and consumes CPU linearly up to the separate memoryLimit while bypassing the configured wall-clock budget.
flaw_origin: Commit e443068cb9281883ff0fe9f755a15f52ada4e7e2 introduced the renderLimit feature and its first enforcement point as ctx.renderLimit.check(performance.now()) inside for (const tpl of templates). The existing for and tablerow tags could pass an empty body array once per collection element, so placing the new security check exclusively inside the zero-trip inner loop created the bypass at the moment the guard was introduced.
ai_marker: absent: BIC commit object e443068cb9281883ff0fe9f755a15f52ada4e7e2 has human author Yang Jun <harttleharttle@gmail.com>, human committer Jun Yang <harttleharttle@gmail.com>, subject/body 'feat: DoS prevention, #250', and no trailers (no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot, or other AI marker).
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/harttle/liquidjs/security/advisories/GHSA-8xx9-69p8-7jp3 identifies <=10.25.7, demonstrates an empty for body taking 2255 ms under renderLimit=50 ms, traces src/tags/for.ts re-entry into Render.renderTemplates(this.templates, ...) for every item, and links fix 5b9c3469085e01c79e2d0af28e2a13f730e1793d. In the validated full-history clone, `git log master -L '/public \* renderTemplates/,/^  }/':src/render/render.ts` and `git log -S 'ctx.renderLimit.check(performance.now())' -- src/render/render.ts` show e443068cb9281883ff0fe9f755a15f52ada4e7e2 first adding the check inside the template-node loop; later commits only change the clock source and unrelated loop state until the fix. `git cat-file -p e443068...` gives sole parent fad00aa14e8beac0514ec4196944b33276f1ff2c and the human-only commit object. Direct parent-tree verification with `git show fad00aa...:src/render/render.ts` shows the same zero-trip template loop without any limiter check, while `git grep -n renderLimit fad00aa... -- src` returns no matches: the renderLimit option and flawed enforcement are absent in the immediate parent. At the BIC, src/tags/for.ts and src/tags/tablerow.ts both build `templates = []` for empty bodies and call renderTemplates(this.templates, ctx, emitter) inside attacker-sized collection loops. `git tag --contains e443068... --sort=version:refname` starts at v10.15.0 and excludes v10.14.0, establishing the feature's first release boundary. `git show 5b9c346...` adds an unconditional `ctx.renderLimit.check(getPerformance().now())` at renderTemplates entry plus empty-for and empty-tablerow regressions. `git tag --contains 5b9c346...` starts at v10.26.0 and excludes v10.25.7; resolved release commits are v10.25.7=34877950bfd0f88666f4ef61f7704defdea546b0 and v10.26.0=c20c0af02d33e8d2ca6b08925eadca8755257c39. The origin issue https://github.com/harttle/liquidjs/issues/250 records the human maintainer's investigation and July 2024 announcement of the DoS feature. The BIC is a normal one-parent commit, not a merge/squash aggregate with reconstructable member commits, so no decomposition applies.
reasoning: The vulnerability is not merely that large loops existed; it is that the newly documented renderLimit security control claimed a per-render time bound but its only check was conditional on rendering at least one body node. Empty loop bodies made that condition false on every iteration while the outer for/tablerow machinery continued, producing the advisory's availability attack. History isolates e443068cb9281883ff0fe9f755a15f52ada4e7e2 as the smallest real BIC because it simultaneously introduced renderLimit and wrote the exact misplaced check; older loop machinery alone could not bypass a control that did not yet exist. The immediate parent has neither renderLimit nor the check, and the first containing release is v10.15.0. Fix 5b9c3469085e01c79e2d0af28e2a13f730e1793d makes the check unconditional at method entry and first ships in v10.26.0 after the advisory's last affected v10.25.7 boundary. AI attribution is decided only from the BIC commit object: it contains human author/committer identities and no AI trailer or bot marker. The Cursor co-authorship trailer on the 2026 fix is explicitly irrelevant to BIC attribution. Therefore the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
